children: Nickel fell below $15,300 per tonne, hitting its lowest level since December 2025, as concerns over a global surplus continued to weigh on prices.
The International Nickel Study Group revised its 2026 outlook from a 32,000-tonne deficit to a 19,000-tonne surplus and expects the excess to widen to 70,000 tonnes in 2027.

At the same time, Indonesian nickel ore imports from the Philippines increased 65.75% year-on-year to 13.52 million tonnes in January-August 2026, with the additional supply helping Indonesian smelters secure feedstock and cushioning the impact of production restrictions.

Meanwhile, Indonesia’s nickel smelter association forecasts a 3.5%-4% decline in domestic nickel product output this year, citing raw-material shortages, higher ore prices, drought-related water constraints, and some smelters redirecting power to aluminum.

title: Nickel Hits Lowest Since December 2025
